arxiv-1811-01472.title: RePair in Compressed Space and Time
arxiv-1811-01472.creator: Kensuke Sakai, Tatsuya Ohno, Keisuke Goto, Yoshimasa Takabatake, Tomohiro I, Hiroshi Sakamoto
arxiv-1811-01472.description: Abstract Given a string T \mathit{T} of length N N , the goal of grammar compression is to construct a small context-free grammar generating only T \mathit{T} . Among existing grammar compression methods, RePair (recursive paring) [Larsson and Moffat, 1999] is notable for achieving good compression ratios in practice.

arxiv-1909-00442.title: Learning Local Forward Models on Unforgiving Games PubID: pubid: 978-1-7281-1884-0/19/$31.00 ©2019 IEEE
arxiv-1909-00442.creator: Alexander Dockhorn, Simon M. Lucas, Vanessa Volz, Ivan Bravi, Raluca D. Gaina, Diego Perez-Liebana
arxiv-1909-00442.description: Abstract This paper examines learning approaches for forward models based on local cell transition functions. We provide a formal definition of local forward models for which we propose two basic learning approaches. Our analysis is based on the game Sokoban, where a wrong action can lead to an unsolvable game state.

arxiv-2307-13087.title: Jointly Equivariant Dynamics for Interacting Particles
arxiv-2307-13087.creator: Alain Ajami, Jean-Paul Gauthier, Francesco Rossi
arxiv-2307-13087.description: Abstract Let a finite set of interacting particles be given, together with a symmetry Lie group G G . Here we describe all possible dynamics that are jointly equivariant with respect to the action of G G . This is relevant e.g., when one aims to describe collective dynamics that are independent of any coordinate change or external influence.

arxiv-2309-03079.title: GPT-InvestAR: Enhancing Stock Investment Strategies through Annual Report Analysis with Large Language Models
arxiv-2309-03079.creator: Udit Gupta
arxiv-2309-03079.description: Abstract Annual Reports of publicly listed companies contain vital information about their financial health which can help assess the potential impact on Stock price of the firm. These reports are comprehensive in nature, going up to, and sometimes exceeding, 100 pages. Analysing these reports is cumbersome even for a single firm, let alone the whole universe of firms that exist.

arxiv-2405-04947.title: The Spectral Gap of a Gaussian Quantum Markovian Generator
arxiv-2405-04947.creator: F. Fagnola, D. Poletti, E. Sasso, V. Umanità
arxiv-2405-04947.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by F. Fagnola, D. Poletti, E. Sasso, V. Umanità. Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups are the natural non-commutative extension of classical Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroups. They arise in open quantum systems of bosons where canonical non-commuting random variables of positions and momenta come into play.

arxiv-2501-01628.creator: Stefan Zellmann
arxiv-2501-01628.description: Abstract 3D visualization and rendering in HPC are very heterogenous applications, though fundamentally the tasks involved are well-defined and do not differ much from application to application. The Khronos Group’s ANARI standard seeks to consolidate 3D rendering across sci-vis applications.

arxiv-2504-14911.title: Lusztig sheaves, decomposition rule and restriction rule Thanks: The author is supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant No. 1288201] and [Grant No. 12471030].
arxiv-2504-14911.creator: Yixin Lan
arxiv-2504-14911.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yixin Lan. In this article, we realize the subquotient based modules of certain tensor products or restricted modules via Lusztig’s perverse sheaves on multi-framed quivers, and provide a construction of their canonical bases. As an application, we prove that the decomposition and restriction coefficients of symmetric Kac-Moody algebras equal to the dimensions of top Borel-Moore homology groups for certain locally closed subsets of Nakajima’s quiver varieties. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary 17B37; Secondary 14D21, 16G20.

arxiv-2509-07749.title: A local generalisation of frame bundles
arxiv-2509-07749.creator: Jérémie Pierard de Maujouy,
arxiv-2509-07749.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jérémie Pierard de Maujouy,. Frame bundles equipped with a principal connection have their local structure characterised by a 1 1 -form, called the Cartan connection 1 1 -form, which gathers the principal connection form and the soldering form. We introduce generalised frame bundles as a smooth manifold equipped with a coframe with value in a suitable Lie algebra and which furthermore satisfies a weakened version of the Maurer-Cartan equation. From this structure it is possible to construct a Lie algebra action on the manifold.

arxiv-2512-09956.title: The Two-Step Property and the Mathematics of Musical Scale Size
arxiv-2512-09956.creator: Emily Clader, Vanessa Jelmyer
arxiv-2512-09956.description: Abstract . A Pythagorean scale is a mathematical encoding of a musical scale as a finite list of numbers of the form 3 b / 2 a 3^{b}/2^{a} . Previous work of the first author introduced the 2-step property as a way to measure which Pythagorean scales are the most “evenly-spaced.

arxiv-2601-14449.title: Top-Quark Pair Production in Heavy-Ion Collisions in the ATLAS Experiment
arxiv-2601-14449.creator: \firstname Patrycja \lastname Potępa \fnsep on behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2601-14449.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by \firstname Patrycja \lastname Potępa \fnsep on behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration. Top-quark pair production in heavy-ion collisions provides a unique opportunity to probe nuclear parton distribution functions and study the time evolution of strongly interacting matter, including the quark-gluon plasma. This work presents the observation and measurement of top-quark pair production in both proton–lead ( p p +Pb) and lead–lead (Pb+Pb) collisions using the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).

pmc-10570551.creator: Alexander Fröhlich, Lauren S. Hughes, Ben Middlehurst, Abigail L. Pfaff, Vivien J. Bubb, Sulev Koks, John P. Quinn
pmc-10570551.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundSINE-VNTR-Alu (SVA) retrotransposons are hominid-specific elements which have been shown to play important roles in processes such as chromatin structure remodelling and regulation of gene expression demonstrating that these repetitive elements exert regulatory functions.
